steps.text: Stir together papaya, orange juice, and pectin in a very large pot over medium-high heat until it begins to boil. Stir constantly as the mixture heats. Once boiling, stir in the sugar, and return to a boil, stirring constantly. Once the jam has returned to a boil, start a timer, and boil for exactly 1 minute.
Ladle the hot jam into the hot, sterilized canning jars and seal with lids and rings. Allow to cool to room temperature, and refrigerate any jars that do not seal.

review.reviewBody: Yummy! I didn't have any orange juice so I used lime in its place I really liked the different flavor.

I do a lot of canning. I mashed the papaya up by pulsing the food processor after I peeled the fruit. Also, I have Amish cookbooks and they recommend using jello in place of pectin; it's cheaper and adds a pretty color. If you do this, be aware that the color jello you use will affect the results. Use 'orange' for this recipe, not lime. If you use the jello, for 5 cups of sugar, I'd recommend taking about 1/2 cup out because the jello has sugar in it and it will be a little too sweet otherwise. Leave the OJ out. Also, I noticed some c/o the jam being a little runny. The Amish book I have recommends freezing fruit before use. Has something to do with the pectin levels (better consistency). Also, for you that have papaya trees and are running over in fruit, my suggestion is "have you ever made homemade wine"? I started making it due to an over abundance of fruit from when I lived in the Apple Valley in Washington. I gave the recipe 4 stars. It was ok, but if I would have lessened the sugar, I think it would have been better (I did not lessen to 4.5 cups & jello has sugar). The flavor was ok, but not as good as I'd like; however, the person on here that suggested habanero peppers..not a bad idea. Kicking it up a notch in that way would be an added punch to regular pepper jelly; if you haven't tried it, do. Nice holiday gift with cream cheese & crackers. Habanero are hot, so if you don't like it really hot try serrano &/or jalapeno. Serrano have really good flavor.

This is a great jam. However, it can be improved upon. I like my jam with a little more zestiness. So, instead of using orange juice I have used lilikoi juice (which is a Hawaiian passionfruit). That is fabulous. People keep telling me to eat papaya with lime juice, so I just tried that - substituting the orange juice with lime juice. Also great. Both make the jam 'pop'. yum.

yummy! The only change i made (because we like sweet and spicy) was to add 2 habeneros. It came out so good. I had got a bunch of papayas from the local food bank and had no idea what to do with them. By happy chance, my grandmother had just given me a bunch of old canning jars. so now i have several batches of Delicious Habenero-Papaya jam and a few batches of regular will be made up tomorrow. It didn't take too long, because i had 3 little helpers to mash the papayas for me. This recipe is definately a keeper

Nice jam! I had some fresh tangerines on hand so I squeezed a couple of them in instead of orange juice... delicious. A great way to take advantage of the giant papayas that go on sale in the Mexican market. The color is gorgeous.

I made this jam 3 days ago. It was very easy and the only change I made was that I squeezed juice from half a lemon to balance out the sweetness. It tasted wonderful but like the previous comments it didn't set up firm enough.

I LOVE making this jam. I use my Pampered Chef cooking blender and I use that. I also use low sugar/no sugar pectin and cut the sugar to 2 cups. It’s SO AMAZING! I just realized the person who authored its name is Angel. My nick name is too! Lol Thank you for this YUMMY recipe!
I used blood orange for the colour
Fantastic. I’ve made it several times. Always beautiful and delicious.
It didn't gel like it should have. I needed more pectin. However I will make it again with the extra pectin because it tastes delicious!!! It worked really good as it was as a sauce on ice-cream.

this jam came out great i have a papaya tree in my back yard and this was my first time making any kind of jam it was so easy the only change i made was i diddnt have pectin so i substituted arrowroot starch it worked like a charm i tried the plate in the freezer trick and it instantly jelled up we tried the papaya as it is in fruit form but my husband diddnt care for it this way so i first made a papaya bread wich came out great and then i tried this jam im so glad i did now i can make several different variations and try new flavors !
Just finished making Jam !, have loads of papayas from the Florida keys ,,,,made with lime juice, jars are fill and are hot and I can hardly wait to cool !,,,
Very nice flavour, but didn't set too well. I keep the jars in the fridge so this helps keep the jam firm enough. Great as an icecream topping.

Excellent taste very easy to make. i am a novice at this jelly thing and i found it so easy to make. i changed it up alittle bit though, i added some pineapple puree to it and about 10 whole habaneros with excellent results
